chosen: Clip-first composition data model: one video is multiple clips, and each clip owns local anchors plus multi-kind tracks including tts, subtitle_timeline, and subtitle.
why: The current v2 model flattened all authoring tracks at the composition level, which makes AI write the whole video at once and caused dirty TTS/subtitle duplication. The new model makes clip the AI authoring unit and keeps TTS-generated timing in a dedicated track.
changed_from: v0.20.0 verified flat tracks with global anchors. v0.21.0 changes the authoring model itself.

constraints.no_vanity: PM-visible effect is a left clip list where each clip previews as a video segment and expands into local tracks.
constraints.no_overreach: This version refactors composition authoring and TTS/subtitle timeline flow only; no new visual component marketplace or cloud export.
constraints.no_rush: Old public episode/clips wording is removed instead of patched around; v3 is the only documented authoring path.
constraints.must_verify: Acceptance is CLI verify/export plus desktop UI evidence that clips and clip-local tracks render.

success_picture: A PM opens the editor, sees several clips on the left, clicks one clip, sees that clip's component/tts/subtitle_timeline/subtitle tracks, previews it, and exports a full MP4 from the same v3 JSON.
risks: Compiler flattening can break preview/export if local clip anchors are resolved incorrectly.
Frontend currently normalizes runtime source into clips, so it needs raw v3 composition context for clip list and clip-local timeline.
Verifier must stop treating top-level tracks as the only source of truth.
